As of April 15, 2026: In April 2026, a San Bernardino County CalFresh applicant does not return requested verification within ten days. Under the Early Denial Waiver, can San Bernardino deny the application before the 30th day?
A. No: San Bernardino is authorized to use the waiver only from June 1, 2026
B. Yes, after 20 days
C. No: no county may deny before the 30th day
D. Yes: all counties have used it since May 1, 2024
E. Yes: it was added on April 20, 2026

As of July 15, 2026: In July 2026, a Santa Barbara County CalFresh applicant does not return requested verification within ten days of the request. Can the county deny the application before the 30th day?
A. Only for expedited applications
B. No: Santa Barbara is not a waiver county
C. Yes, but only after an agency conference
D. Yes: Santa Barbara has operated the Early Denial Waiver since June 1, 2026
E. No: denial must wait until the 30th day

A. $199

As of February 1, 2026: A two-person household in one of the 48 states (a 67-year-old and her 64-year-old husband, not categorically eligible) has $2,500 a month in Social Security, $300 a month in verified medical costs for the 67-year-old, and $1,400 a month in actual shelter costs. Is it eligible, and what is its monthly benefit?
A. Eligible: $54
B. Eligible: $546
C. Eligible: $24 (the minimum)
D. Ineligible: net income is over $1,763
E. Ineligible: gross income is over $2,292

As of February 1, 2026: A two-person household in one of the 48 states with no elderly or disabled members, not categorically eligible, has $2,400 a month in gross earnings and $1,500 in rent. Can it get SNAP?
A. No: its net income is over $1,763
B. Yes: only the net income test applies
C. Yes, if it has under $3,000 in resources
D. No: its gross income is over the $2,292 gross limit, whatever its deductions
E. Yes, because its net income after the shelter deduction is under $1,763

As of February 1, 2026: A 70-year-old living alone in one of the 48 states (not in an initial month) has $1,400 a month in Social Security and pays $700 rent, with no other expenses. Her net income is under the limit but 30 percent of it exceeds the one-person maximum. What benefit does she get?
A. $25
B. $12
C. $0
D. $298
E. $24, the minimum allotment

As of February 1, 2026: A homeless four-person household in one of the 48 states (not receiving free shelter; the state offers the homeless shelter deduction) has $1,500 a month in gross earnings and no shelter costs. What is its monthly SNAP benefit?
A. $760
B. $820
C. $759
D. $994
E. $700

As of February 1, 2026: A single mother of two in one of the 48 states earns $2,000 a month and pays $400 a month in child care so she can work. Her rent, including utilities, is $1,002. No one is elderly or disabled. What is the household's monthly SNAP benefit?
A. $459
B. $695
C. $639
D. $589
E. $785

As of February 1, 2026: A four-person household in one of the 48 states (no elderly or disabled members) earns $2,500 a month and pays $1,800 a month in shelter costs including utilities. What is its monthly SNAP benefit?
A. $610
B. $655
C. $734
D. $684
E. $994

As of February 1, 2026: A 45-year-old SNAP recipient who is not disabled has $300 a month in verified prescription costs. How much medical deduction does the household get?
A. $35
B. $300
C. $265 (costs over $35)
D. None: the excess medical deduction is only for elderly or disabled members
E. $150

As of February 1, 2026: A two-person household in one of the 48 states (no elderly or disabled members, not categorically eligible) has $2,200 a month in unemployment benefits and pays $500 a month rent including utilities. Is it eligible?
A. Yes, with the minimum benefit
B. No: its gross income is over the limit
C. Yes: its gross income is under $2,292
